title: Reduction of a derived mate using the unprimed counit
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal A',\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] in a common universe [def-weil-size-convention], with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Write $K^+(\mathcal C)$ for bounded-below cochain complexes modulo chain homotopy, $q:K^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms, and $K(F)$ for termwise application of an additive functor. Let $L:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $L':\mathcal B'\to\mathcal A'$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$ and $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be exact additive functors. Put $E=D(L)$, $E'=D(L')$, $T=D(G)$ and $S=D(H)$, with their canonical natural localization isomorphisms $\phi_{F,V}:D(F)(qV)\xrightarrow{\sim}qK(F)V$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $\sigma:L'G\to HL$ be an arbitrary natural transformation, and let $\sigma^K:K(L')K(G)\to K(H)K(L)$ be its termwise transformation on $K^+$. Assume $\mathcal A,\mathcal A'$ have enough injectives, meaning that every object embeds into an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Give additive right adjoints $R,R'$ and adjunctions $L\dashv R$, $L'\dashv R'$. Write $\eta'^K,\varepsilon^K$ for their termwise homotopy unit and counit [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Let $U=\mathbf R R$, $U'=\mathbf R R'$ with natural comparison maps $\alpha:qK(R)\to Uq$, $\alpha':qK(R')\to U'q$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Use the canonical derived adjunctions $E\dashv U$ and $E'\dashv U'$, with primed unit $\eta'^D$ and unprimed counit $\varepsilon^D$, normalized by the unit and counit identities of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction]. For $N\in K^+(\mathcal B)$ put
$$A_N=\phi_{L',K(G)N}\circ E'(\phi_{G,N}),\qquad B_N=\phi_{H,K(L)N}\circ S(\phi_{L,N}).$$ Let $\theta:E'T\to SE$ be any natural transformation satisfying $B_N\circ\theta_{qN}=q(\sigma^K_N)\circ A_N$ for all $N\in K^+(\mathcal B)$, and write $m:TU\to U'S$ for its mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. For $P\in K^+(\mathcal A)$ put $X=qP$, $N=K(R)P$, $Z=qK(G)N$, $h=\phi_{H,P}$, $t=T(\alpha_P)\circ\phi_{G,N}^{-1}$ and
$$d=K(H)(\varepsilon^K_P)\circ\sigma^K_N:K(L')K(G)N\to K(H)P.$$
Then
$$U'(h)\circ m_X\circ t=U'(q(d))\circ U'(\phi_{L',K(G)N})\circ\eta'^D_Z.$$
This identity is valid for noninvertible $\sigma$, $\alpha_P$, and $\alpha'$, without assuming that $H$ preserves injectives.

source.place: Old proof steps 4 and 5: derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac, lines 439–451 and 454–482 (mate expansion, naturality, counit comparison, and use of hθ).

proof.text:
Put $u=\alpha_P$ and $a=\phi_{G,N}$. By the component definition of the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate],
$$m_X=U'(S(\varepsilon^D_X))\circ U'(\theta_{UX})\circ\eta'^D_{TU X}.$$
Naturality of the unit at $t:Z\to TU X$ gives $\eta'^D_{TU X}\circ t=U'(E'(t))\circ\eta'^D_Z$. Thus
$$U'(h)m_Xt=U'\bigl(h\circ S(\varepsilon^D_X)\circ\theta_{UX}\circ E'(t)\bigr)\circ\eta'^D_Z.$$

source.place: derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac, lines 439–450: hmate and unit naturality h₁; also naturality at the invertible localization component

proof.text:
Since $t=T(u)\circ a^{-1}$, naturality of $\theta$ at $u:qN\to UX$ says
$$\theta_{UX}\circ E'(t)=S(E(u))\circ\theta_{qN}\circ E'(a^{-1}).$$
Consequently the morphism inside $U'$ in Step 1 is
$$h\circ S(\varepsilon^D_X\circ E(u))\circ\theta_{qN}\circ E'(a^{-1}).$$
This uses naturality at a morphism, not inversion of $u$.

source.place: derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac, lines 451 and 461–462: h₂ and its substitution

proof.text:
Set $s=\phi_{L,N}$ and $e=\varepsilon^K_P:K(L)N\to P$. The unprimed counit identity of [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction] at $P$ is
$$\varepsilon^D_X\circ E(u)=q(e)\circ s.$$
Substitution in Step 2 gives the inside morphism
$$h\circ S(q(e))\circ S(s)\circ\theta_{qN}\circ E'(a^{-1}).$$

source.place: derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac, lines 452 and 462: h₃, the unprimed counit comparison

proof.text:
Write $f=\phi_{H,K(L)N}$ and $b=\phi_{L',K(G)N}$. Naturality of the localization comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] at $e$ gives
$$h\circ S(q(e))=q(K(H)(e))\circ f.$$
The assumed square identity is $f\circ S(s)\circ\theta_{qN}=q(\sigma^K_N)\circ b\circ E'(a)$. Therefore the inside morphism of Step 3 equals
$$q(K(H)(e))\circ q(\sigma^K_N)\circ b\circ E'(a)\circ E'(a^{-1})=q(d)\circ b.$$
Here functoriality cancels only $a\circ a^{-1}$ and combines the two localized homotopy morphisms.

source.place: derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac, lines 459–460 and 467–482: h₈, h₉ and the key equality

proof.text:
Insert $q(d)\circ b$ into Step 1 and use functoriality of $U'$:
$$U'(h)\circ m_X\circ t=U'(q(d))\circ U'(\phi_{L',K(G)N})\circ\eta'^D_Z.$$
No step inverts $\sigma$, $u$, or $\alpha'$, and no step requires $K(H)P$ to consist of injectives.
